results.label: this tree ships the plan gate (src/bots/plan-gate.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the app’s own starter playbook is published active (the sample this section measures)
with several active plans the gate reports `ambiguous` and names every candidate, and it NEVER picks one silently
and the endpoint publishes the vocabulary this app enforces, with a concrete line per fact
the limits travel with it, so a client cannot present the gate as a performance or broker claim
an analysis run before the trader has decided is served `ambiguous` (with the names) and gates nothing
pausing them all returns the analysis to `no_plan`, which blocks nothing — a plan is not required to use the app
and the candidates are identical to the ones the ambiguous run produced: an unconsulted gate forbids nothing
a published plan is read back with its lines classified: enforced, prose, unrecognised
and it carries the M102 version the rules were saved as
the analysis confirms against that plan: the payload names it, its version and how many requirements are enforced
a requirement the candidate cannot meet REFUSES it, with the refusal as the first reason
the candidate carries the rule-by-rule result beside the refusal, so the trader sees which box was not checked
and the verdict does not arm the side the plan refused
with exactly one active plan the gate uses it without being asked (and says which one)
a requirement the candidate meets leaves it tradeable and does not touch its grade or score
two plans really are active before the ambiguity is measured (the state being tested, not an assumption)
two active plans are reported as `ambiguous` WITH both names, and NOTHING is gated on a guess
naming one resolves it, so the ambiguity is a one-click fix rather than a dead end
pausing every plan returns the gate to `no_plan` — a paused plan is not silently applied
while naming a paused plan still works, because that is the trader asking for it by name
another trader’s plan id is a 404 on the gate reader — never a fallback to their own plan
and the same id on the analyse route is refused too, so a signal cannot be confirmed against a plan the caller does not own
a malformed id is a 400 with the gate’s own code, not an internal error
and a fractional or negative id is refused the same way
the chart endpoint confirms against the SAME plan the analysis did (M124’s rule: not a second opinion)
a scan row carries the plan it was confirmed against and whether the plan took that setup away
the trader’s own webhook token is issued and analysis is on for it (the state this section measures)
an alert analysed while a plan is active is confirmed against that plan, and the alert carries the gate back with it
and the plan REFUSED the alert: no signal is created from it, because the refusal reaches the verdict the auto-create rule reads
the alert history serves that gate as an OBJECT the panel can read (the stored JSON text is parsed on the way out, like the sibling alerts route)
with a different plan active the same alert is confirmed against THAT plan — the alert is gated by the plan the trader is running now, not by a preference baked into the alert
and with no plan active the alert says `no_plan` and blocks nothing — an incoming alert is not refused for the absence of a plan
a plan written in prose has ZERO enforced requirements, and says so rather than looking satisfied
and the prose plan refuses nothing: free text is never interpreted, in either direction
the free-text `market_conditions` field is reported as NOT parsed — "ranging only" cannot silently become a rule
rules stored double-encoded (a client echoing the stored string back at a route that stringifies its input) are reported as malformed, not shown as a satisfied plan
and that plan refuses nothing while it cannot be read — the trader sees the reason to re-save instead of a silently empty checklist
the app’s own starter rows are a list of lines, so the sample this probe measures is not itself the malformed case
editing the rules changes what the gate enforces, and the M102 version moves with it
analysing with a plan writes exactly what analysing without one writes — the gate adds no row of its own
and reading the plan never rewrites it: `strategies` and its M102 history are byte-identical across the gate read
the milestone adds NO table, index or trigger of its own — the plan lives in `strategies` exactly as before

scope: M56 api: the written plan over the real routes, its ownership and its read-only proof: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
